nodes.label: 4iCreative Limited
nodes.rationale: HK event production company (CR 2336607, InnoCentre tenant, HKSTP category 'Design') organising accredited CME events under HKCP and HKCR. Not a product competitor: no software engineering capacity, no product, no repos -- a people-and-craft business scaling linearly with headcount.

nodes.label: A company's self-description is evidence of how it wants to be bought
nodes.rationale: Their site claims medical-communications work; first-hand attendance showed event production. Third-party categorisation (HKSTP 'Design'), hiring (Design/Graphics/Multimedia), and portfolio artefacts (posters, photography) all supported the corrected read and were under-weighted on first pass. When those disagree with the homepage, the homepage is the outlier.

nodes.label: Four-level evidence legend (verified / reported / inferred / false)
nodes.rationale: Marks every claim by how it was obtained -- direct fetch, uncorroborated third-party report, inference, or found-false -- so a later reader can tell which lines carry weight. §8 lists explicitly what was not verified (directors, revenue, true event volume, headcount, site history).

nodes.label: AI-generated WordPress site (ZipWP signature)
nodes.rationale: zipwp/v1 in the REST namespace, every page created in one week, unfilled '+ Events Managed' stat blocks, HTML style markup pasted into a DNS TXT record, and a live-but-empty SureCart shop -- the site was generated, not designed, and the one productisation signal shipped nothing.

nodes.label: Accreditation lead time (~4 weeks apply, ~2 weeks approve)
nodes.rationale: The category and point value come back BEFORE the event, which confirms Stage 7's 'CPD config at event creation' shape rather than a post-hoc assignment.

nodes.label: Accreditation applicant is usually the pharma company itself
nodes.rationale: HKCR 2026 organiser frequency: Novartis 5, Roche 4, Bayer 4, MSD 2, GSK 2, MIMS 2, 4iCreative 1 -- sometimes an agency, sometimes a society. Bears directly on B2's organisers model and on the open 'who pays' question.

nodes.label: The collateral production mechanism
nodes.rationale: Organiser assembles content -> production company lays it out and produces hero art -> frozen PDF hand-versioned by filename (YYMMDD + revision letter) -> email blast with N attachments -> any change means a new revision letter, a new blast, and two versions in the wild. The competitive question turned out less interesting than this mechanism.

nodes.label: ICI Summit 2026 (three real event artefacts)
nodes.rationale: Three documents, three sources, three production signatures: a poster+agenda from the production company, a Word-to-PDF accreditation sheet from the organiser, and a 14-page transportation slide deck from the venue that misspells the event name. The production company touched one of three, and on that one contributed hero artwork plus layout applied to organiser-supplied data.

nodes.label: Six failure modes of frozen hand-versioned PDFs
nodes.rationale: Stale by construction (poster frozen one day before accreditation issued, so the attendee's most important information could not be on the most-distributed artefact), no single source of truth, no personalisation, revision fan-out, dead-end artefacts that cannot update or check anyone in, and logistics trapped in a slide export.

nodes.label: Existing poster route as displacement beachhead
nodes.rationale: app/(public)/events/[id]/poster/page.tsx already exists -- 351 lines, print-aware light-always --po-* tokens because it prints on paper, embeds the event QR via buildEventQrPng, derives speakers from agenda_blocks. ~90% of the real poster is renderable from data Eventar holds or nearly holds; the missing pieces are per-session sponsor attribution, a tiered logo asset library, and the accreditation table. The hero illustration is the only irreducibly bespoke element.

nodes.label: Why an agency cannot copy the replacement
nodes.rationale: Their revenue depends on revision being expensive. A mechanism where revision is free cannot be offered by a business that bills per revision -- a business-model constraint, not a competence gap, and therefore the more durable kind of advantage. The displacement target is not to out-design them but to reduce their design job to supplying one hero image.

nodes.label: Design as the acquisition surface
nodes.rationale: Compliance infrastructure is a slow, trust-heavy, hard-to-demo sale; collateral generation is wanted within 30 seconds of being seen. Design pulls the integrity product in behind it. The threat from the agency is commercial rather than technical -- budget interposition and channel lock-out, neither of which requires them to build anything.

nodes.label: Credit is (event, body, days_attended), not (event, attendance)
nodes.rationale: The ICI accreditation PDF awards credit from one event to thirteen bodies, differentiated per day -- the same two days yield 11 to a pathologist, 9 to a physician, 5 to an O&G. Multi-college is the norm at conference scale, so 'HKCP as first accrediting body' describes one row of thirteen on a real event. Whether award_attendance_credit() can express this is inferred from PROJECT_STATE, NOT verified against the migration.

nodes.label: Per-activity caps live on the body, not the event
nodes.rationale: Community Medicine, O&G and Paediatricians each cap below the sum of their own per-day awards. That is the structural justification for body_rules being versioned append-only and separate from event config, and a live specification for B3's bounded grammar: per-body rate, per-segment award, per-activity ceiling. Notably nothing here needs a general rules engine.
